title: The greatest is charity (1 Corinthians 13:13)
hook: faith, hope, charity remain, and the greatest is charity
tomorrow: you reach the top. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Simeon's song: rest, because the promise has been seen. The line was in peace. Today, the second-to-last step, and a ranking Paul makes himself.

Moving out comes down to boxes. What goes in the car, what goes to a cousin, what goes to the curb. You find out fast what you actually need. Paul does the same packing with the whole spiritual life, in the Douay-Rheims: "And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity." Three things make it into the last box. And he ranks them. Faith carried the path, hope anchored it. So why does love win?
screen: `WHAT GOES IN THE LAST BOX?` → `THESE THREE REMAIN.` → `WHY DOES LOVE WIN?`

segments.voice: Paul gives the reason a few verses earlier: "Charity never falleth away." Prophecies end, knowledge passes, but love doesn't. Catholic readers, following Thomas Aquinas, draw it out. Faith is trusting what you can't yet see; one day, they say, it gives way to seeing. Hope reaches for what you don't yet have; one day it gives way to having. Love doesn't give way to anything. It's the one thing you already do now that you'll still be doing then. That's why it's the greatest: it's the only one that comes all the way through. And it doesn't stay a private virtue. The Second Vatican Council, writing about people of every religion, began from one human family: all peoples share one origin, it said, because God made the whole human race to live on the face of the earth, and share one final goal, God himself. Then it drew the conclusion: we can't truly call on God as Father of all while refusing to treat any person as a brother or sister. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Church's document on other religions begins from one human race, not from what divides it. That's charity at full width. The greatest of these isn't greatest because it's loudest. It's greatest because it lasts, and because it leaves nobody outside.
screen: `CHARITY NEVER FALLETH AWAY.` · `FAITH GIVES WAY TO SEEING.` · `LOVE IS THE ONE THAT LASTS.` · `ONE HUMAN RACE, ONE ORIGIN.` · then, large: `THE GREATEST OF THESE.`

segments.voice: Find a photo of someone you love, or just bring their face to mind, and look at it for a while without hurrying. Let one loving thing you could do for them this week come into focus, as small or plain as it wants to be. If you pray, you can hold them before God in silence; that's enough.
The greatest is charity. Of faith, hope and love, the one that never falls away, and leaves nobody outside.
The line to keep: the greatest of these, because love is what you'll still be doing when you arrive. See you at the top.

chat.meaning: Faith and hope carry you; charity is what remains. Paul calls it the greatest because it never falls away, so the loving act comes first.

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an older English Catholic translation of the Bible

Thomas Aquinas.meaning: a medieval Dominican theologian and Doctor of the Church

Second Vatican Council.meaning: a council of the world's bishops held in Rome

charity.meaning: the love that loves God and every neighbor
